label: rare: first copy step reading z/e, or original token right after i
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps, about 0.3% of sequences) with weak activations (max 0.23). Two loose loci: (a) the first copy step (recall_idx 1, input = orig(0)), mostly when the input is z or e, and more often when the next output is 0, q, 1 or z; (b) original-phase steps t=3..6 directly after an i, especially when 0 and i appear earlier (e.g. 0 0 i [e], z 0 0 i [h]). Together these hold about 74% of activation mass, but they over-predict roughly 80x (dev precision about 1%). Tightening with next_out or seen(0) gets precision only to 5-13% and costs most of the recall. Almost never fires at t<2, on the delimiter, or after copying has gone wrong. No simple predicate tells firing contexts apart from the many identical-looking contexts where it stays silent, and magnitude does not follow any variable that was checked.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+5.45), orig0=z (+4.68), prev_tok=i (+4.45), phase=2 & in_tok=e (+3.78), orig0=e (+3.43), orig1=q (+3.08). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-3.66), prev3_tok=- (-2.56), prev2_tok=q (-2.12).
